title: Hirmenschelis: John's testament family
standfirst: John's 1577 administration records a widow and two children, but not a burgh pedigree. A separately supplied Huchesoun strip is an archival lead, not proof of kinship.
question: Was the Hirmenschelis testator the John in the burgh protocols, and can the Huchesoun fragment help identify Margaret?
answer: The testament confirms John as father of Katherine and Marjory, following the accepted reading, and records Margaret as widow. It does not identify John's father, prove Margaret's modern surname or maternity, or connect Andro Huchesoun's partially read confirmation to this family.

chapters.title: A small family at administration
body: The Edinburgh Commissary record and its index place the testament at Hirmenschelis and 4 May 1577.
Katherine and Marjory are the accepted named children. Margaret's surname remains a qualified palaeographical reading rather than a confirmed identity.

chapters.title: The Huchesoun strip remains separate
body: The same supplied PDF includes a separate Andro Huchesoun confirmation, partially transcribed with children and a provisional Johne Huchesoun.
Its attachment to image 276 and the unfinished grammar have not established either a record relationship or a Glasgow family relationship.
